name: Wiesing
kurzbeschreibung: Luxurious residential community in the Zillertal at the confluence of the Zillertal and Inntal, offering breathtaking views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Wiesing is situated at an elevation of 566 metres above sea level in the Lower Inn Valley within the Schwaz district of Tyrol, strategically positioned at the crossroads connecting the Inn Valley, the entrance to the Zillertal, and the alpine ascent toward Lake Achensee. Home to approximately 2,200 residents, this peaceful settlement rests upon a sunny moraine plateau at the foot of the rugged Rofan mountains northeast of the River Inn. Thanks to its prime geographical location, Wiesing serves as a vital transport junction where the federal highways toward Bavaria and the Zillertal diverge. Despite this excellent connectivity, Wiesing preserves the tranquil ambience of a genuine Tyrolean country village, providing a scenic gateway for leisurely riverside cycling, hikes into the Rofan range, and excursions to Tyrol's largest lake.

Geschichte

The settlement's name dates back to early Bavarian colonisation, derived from the Germanic clan leader Wisso, translating to 'settlement of Wisso's kin'. The village was documented as early as 930 AD in records of the Archbishopric of Salzburg when a noblewoman named Himildrud donated estates to the church. During the 15th and 16th centuries, Wiesing prospered from the regional silver boom in neighbouring Schwaz. In 1504, during the Landshut War of Succession, Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I ordered the construction of a powder magazine (Pulverturm) adjacent to the churchyard, remnants of which survive today. The parish church dedicated to Saints Martin and Nicholas features a 14th-century Gothic tower, while its nave was rebuilt in graceful Rococo style between 1777 and 1781. In 1889, the opening of the Achensee Railway inaugurated Europe's oldest surviving steam cog railway.

Anreise

Wiesing enjoys some of the finest transport connections in central Tyrol. Motorists access the village directly from the Inntal Autobahn A12 via the Wiesing/Zillertal/Achensee motorway interchange, or toll-free along the federal highway B171. At the town entrance, the Achensee highway B181 towards Lake Tegernsee and Munich and the Zillertal highway B169 through the Brettfall Tunnel diverge. Rail travelers arrive via the major railway junction in Jenbach, situated just two kilometres away, where mainline Austrian Federal Railways trains (Railjet, ICE, Nightjet) connect with the narrow-gauge Zillertal Railway and the historic metre-gauge Achensee Railway. From Jenbach railway station, frequent regional bus services of the Verkehrsverbund Tirol (lines 4080 and 8332) reach Wiesing village centre within five minutes.

Tipps

A highlight for railway and heritage enthusiasts is a journey aboard the historic Achensee Railway (Achenseebahn): dating from 1889, Europe's oldest steam-driven cog railway chugs up the slopes above Wiesing towards Maurach and Seespitz, connecting directly with steamboats on Lake Achensee. Mountain hikers can embark directly from the village along scenic paths into the Rofan mountains, including challenging ascents up the Ebner Joch (2,055 m). Perched dramatically on a rocky promontory overlooking the valley entrance, the pilgrimage church of Maria Brettfall provides an unforgettable viewpoint spanning the Inn and Zillertal valleys. For cyclists, Wiesing serves as an ideal hub directly linking the flat Inn Cycle Path (R3) with the family-friendly Zillertal Cycle Path along the rivers.
